s: Pisirodus is son of Callipatira
q: And Pisirodus her son having been victorious

s: Olympia has river Alpheus (a full and very pleasant river immediately visible there)
q: And when you have got to Olympia immediately you see the river Alpheus, a full and very pleasant river

s: Alpheus is a river (with seven notable tributaries)
q: And when you have got to Olympia immediately you see the river Alpheus, a full and very pleasant river, and no less than seven notable rivers are tributaries to it.

s: Alpheus rises in Arcadia (not in Elis)
q: And the source of the Alpheus is in Arcadia and not in Elis.

s: Alpheus receives tributary Cladeus (from Elis)
q: and the Cladeus from Elis also contributes its stream.

s: Ortygia is near Syracuse (an island)
q: she crossed over they say to an island near Syracuse, called Ortygia

s: Olympian games are held every fifth year (according to the tradition of Idæan Hercules)
q: He appointed them to be held every fifth year because he and his brothers were five in number.

s: Cronos has temple at Olympia (built by mortals of the golden age)
q: and that he had a temple built to him at Olympia by the mortals who then lived, who were called the golden age

s: Rhea entrusts Zeus (to the Idæan Dactyli when he was a boy)
q: when Zeus was born, Rhea entrusted the charge of the boy to the Idæan Dactyli, who were otherwise called the Curetes

s: Olympian contests are instituted by Idæan Hercules (who gave them their name)
q: At any rate to Idæan Hercules belongs the glory that he first instituted and gave their name to the Olympian contests.

s: Apollo is victorious at Olympia (in racing and boxing contests)
q: Other gods are said to have been victorious, as Apollo who outran Hermes, who challenged him to the contest, and outboxed Ares.

s: Antigonus is a king of the Macedonians
q: partly through the assistance of Antigonus the son of Demetrius, who was king of the Macedonians.

s: Olympia hosts Olympian games (as the venue of the contests)
q: And after this they say Clymenus the son of Cardys, (in the 50th year after Deucalion’s flood), a descendant of Idæan Hercules, came from Crete and established games at Olympia

s: Olympian Zeus has contest at Olympia (the contest was made famous by Pelops)
q: And a generation after Endymion, Pelops made the contest to Olympian Zeus more famous than any of his predecessors.

s: Elis dislikes horse (as a longstanding disposition)
q: the people of Elis (who have always disliked the horse) yoke two mules together instead of horses.

s: Elis has tribes 12 (in the 103rd Olympiad)
q: And in the 103rd Olympiad, as the people of Elis had 12 tribes, a general Umpire was appointed by each.

s: Elis has tribes 8 (after losing territory in war with the Arcadians)
q: And when they were hard pressed by the Arcadians in war, they lost a portion of their territory and all the villages in this portion, and so they were only 8 tribes in number in the 104th Olympiad

s: Iphitus renewed Olympian games (after their suspension)
q: And after the reign of Oxylus, who also established games, the Olympian games were suspended till Iphitus. And when he renewed the games as I have before stated

s: Iphitus was umpire of Olympian games (the sole original umpire)
q: for Iphitus was the only umpire, and after Iphitus the posterity of Oxylus

s: Iphitus is depicted being crowned by Ecechiria (in the temple at Olympia)
q: as you enter the brazen doors on the right in front of the pillar is Iphitus being crowned by his wife Ecechiria

s: Olympian games were suspended until Iphitus (after the reign of Oxylus)
q: And after the reign of Oxylus, who also established games, the Olympian games were suspended till Iphitus.

s: Olympian games included first running (when continuously revived)
q: From the time that the Olympian games were revived continuously, prizes were first instituted for running

s: Olympia contains Temple of Zeus at Olympia
q: And the temple and statue of Zeus were built out of the spoils of Pisa, which the people of Elis razed to the ground, after quelling the revolt of Pisa and some of the neighbouring towns that revolted with Pisa.

s: Olympian games included double course (later added to the programme)
q: And in the 14th Olympiad afterwards the double course was introduced

s: Olympian games included pentathlum (later added to the programme)
q: And in the 18th Olympiad they remembered the pentathlum and the wrestling

s: Olympian games included boxing (later added to the programme)
q: And in the 23rd Olympiad they ordained prizes for boxing

s: Olympian games included race of full-grown horses (later added to the programme)
q: And in the 25th Olympiad they had a race of full-grown horses

s: Olympian games included pancratium (later added to the programme)
q: And in the eighth Olympiad later they introduced the pancratium and the riding race.

s: Olympian games included contest of the boys (instituted by the people of Elis)
q: And the contest of the boys was not a revival of ancient usage, but the people of Elis instituted it because the idea pleased them.

s: Olympian games included race in heavy armour (as an exercise for war)
q: And the race in heavy armour was tried in the 65th Olympiad, as an exercise for war I think

s: Olympian games included race of two full-grown horses (also called a pair)
q: And the race of two full-grown horses called a pair was established in the 93rd Olympiad

s: Olympian games included race of a pair of colts (later established)
q: And they afterwards established races of a pair of colts and for riding a colt

s: Olympian games institutes a pancratium-contest for boys (in the 145th Olympiad)
q: And in the 145th Olympiad prizes were instituted for a pancratium-contest for boys

s: Olympia contains Altis (the sacred grove of Zeus)
q: And the sacred grove of Zeus they have from old time called Altis, slightly changing the Greek word for grove[69]: it is indeed called Altis also by Pindar, in the Ode he composed for a victor at Olympia.

s: Olympian games discontinued pentathlum for boys (by proclamation of the people of Elis)
q: For the pentathlum for boys was established in the 38th Olympiad, but when the Lacedæmonian Eutelidas had won the crown of wild olive, the people of Elis did not care that their lads should train for the pentathlum. So it dropped.

s: Olympian games discontinued chariot race (in the 84th Olympiad)
q: And the chariot race and the trotting race, the former established in the 70th Olympiad and the latter in the 71st Olympiad, were both stopped by proclamation in the 84th Olympiad.

s: Olympian games discontinued trotting race (in the 84th Olympiad)
q: And the chariot race and the trotting race, the former established in the 70th Olympiad and the latter in the 71st Olympiad, were both stopped by proclamation in the 84th Olympiad.

s: pentathlum is a Olympic contest
q: And in the 18th Olympiad they remembered the pentathlum and the wrestling

s: pentathlum is scheduled before pancratium (in the former arrangement of the games)
q: And at that period the pancratiasts did not appear till night for they could not compete sooner, so much time being taken up by the horse-races and pentathlum.

s: pancratium is a Olympic contest
q: And in the eighth Olympiad later they introduced the pancratium and the riding race.

s: pancratium was scheduled after horse-races (before the programme was rearranged)
q: And at that period the pancratiasts did not appear till night for they could not compete sooner, so much time being taken up by the horse-races and pentathlum.

s: Umpires of Elis numbered 9 (after two umpires had served for a long period)
q: But in the 25th Olympiad afterwards 9 general Umpires were appointed: three for the horse-race, three to watch the pentathlum, and three to preside over the remaining games.

s: Umpires of Elis numbered 10 (after the 9-umpire arrangement)
q: And in the 2nd Olympiad after this a tenth Umpire was appointed.

s: Umpires of Elis numbered 12 (when Elis had 12 tribes)
q: And in the 103rd Olympiad, as the people of Elis had 12 tribes, a general Umpire was appointed by each.

s: Hercules has title Assistant (as an altar title)
q: and erected an altar to his ancestor Hercules and to the other Curetes, giving Hercules the title of Assistant.

s: Umpires of Elis numbered 8 (after Elis lost territory to the Arcadians)
q: and so they were only 8 tribes in number in the 104th Olympiad, and had only 8 general Umpires accordingly.

s: Altis is a sacred grove of Zeus (at Olympia)
q: And the sacred grove of Zeus they have from old time called Altis

s: Zeus has sacred grove Altis (at Olympia)
q: And the sacred grove of Zeus they have from old time called Altis

s: Temple of Zeus at Olympia is a Doric building
q: The temple is a Doric building, and outside it is a colonnade.

s: Temple of Zeus at Olympia has architect Libon (a native of Elis)
q: And its architect was Libon a native of Elis.

s: Temple of Zeus at Olympia has roof tiles of Pentelic marble (marble made to imitate tiles)
q: And the tiles on the roof are not of baked earth, but Pentelican marble to imitate tiles.

s: Temple of Zeus at Olympia depicts chariot race between Pelops and Œnomaus (in bas relief on the gable)
q: And on the gables in bas relief is the chariot race between Pelops and Œnomaus, and both chariots in motion.

s: statue of Zeus is the work of Phidias (shown by the inscription written at its base)
q: that the statue of Zeus was the work of Phidias is shown by the inscription written at the base of it,

s: Phidias is a Athenian (son of Charmides)
q: “Phidias the Athenian, the son of Charmides, made me.”

s: statue of Zeus has inscription Phidias the Athenian, the son of Charmides, made me.
q: “Phidias the Athenian, the son of Charmides, made me.”

s: Hercules has altar at Olympia (an altar was erected to him)
q: and erected an altar to his ancestor Hercules and to the other Curetes, giving Hercules the title of Assistant.

s: chariot race between Pelops and Œnomaus is depicted on Temple of Zeus at Olympia (in bas relief on the gable)
q: And on the gables in bas relief is the chariot race between Pelops and Œnomaus, and both chariots in motion.

s: Œnomaus is depicted with Sterope (on the right of Zeus in the gable sculpture)
q: and on the right hand of Zeus is Œnomaus with a helmet on his head, and beside him his wife Sterope, one of the daughters of Atlas.

s: Œnomaus has charioteer Myrtilus (in the gable sculpture)
q: And Myrtilus, who was the charioteer of Œnomaus, is seated behind the four horses.

s: Labours of Hercules are depicted at Olympia (in bas relief on the temple)
q: There are also in bas relief at Olympia most of the Labours of Hercules.

s: Labours of Hercules include Erymanthian boar (depicted above the temple doors)
q: Above the doors of the temple is the hunting of the Erymanthian boar

s: Labours of Hercules include Diomede (Hercules taking his mares)
q: and Hercules taking the mares of Diomede the Thracian

s: Labours of Hercules include Geryon (Hercules robbing his oxen)
q: and robbing the oxen of Geryon in the island of Erythea

s: Labours of Hercules include Amazon (Hercules robbing her belt)
q: above the chamber behind the doors he is robbing the Amazon of her belt

s: Labours of Hercules include Cretan Minotaur (depicted above the chamber doors)
q: and there is the stag, and the Cretan Minotaur, and the Stymphalian birds, and the hydra, and the Nemean lion.

s: Hercules is a victor in wrestling (at the Olympic contests)
q: It is also recorded of Hercules that he was victorious in wrestling and in the pancratium.

s: Hercules is a victor in the pancratium (at the Olympic contests)
q: It is also recorded of Hercules that he was victorious in wrestling and in the pancratium.

s: Hercules has labours depicted at Olympia (in reliefs on the temple)
q: There are also in bas relief at Olympia most of the Labours of Hercules.

s: Pelops made famous Olympian Zeus (the contest at Olympia)
q: And a generation after Endymion, Pelops made the contest to Olympian Zeus more famous than any of his predecessors.

s: Ptolemy is son of Philip (according to the Macedonians, by birth)
q: Ptolemy, the Macedonians think, was really the son of Philip the son of Amyntas, (but putatively the son of Lagus), for his mother, they say, was pregnant when she was given to Lagus to wife by Philip.

s: Seleucus is son of Antiochus
q: welcomed Seleucus the son of Antiochus, a fugitive who had been driven into exile by Antigonus

s: Seleucus is exiled by Antigonus (as a fugitive)
q: welcomed Seleucus the son of Antiochus, a fugitive who had been driven into exile by Antigonus

s: Antigonus is father of Demetrius
q: handing them over to his son Demetrius, a boy in years a man in intellect

s: Demetrius is son of Antigonus (a boy in years, a man in intellect)
q: handing them over to his son Demetrius, a boy in years a man in intellect

s: Ptolemy resists those who wished to give all the dominions of Alexander to Aridæus the son of Philip (upon the death of Alexander)
q: And upon the death of Alexander, he it was who mainly resisted those who wished to give all the dominions of Alexander to Aridæus the son of Philip, and he again was responsible for the different nationalities being divided into kingdoms.

s: Antigonus loses forces the greater part of his forces (after fighting Lysimachus and Cassander and the army of Seleucus)
q: And Antigonus, though unsuccessful with Rhodes and Egypt, ventured not long afterwards to fight against Lysimachus and Cassander and the army of Seleucus, and lost the greater part of his forces, and himself died mainly from being worn out by the length of the war against Eumenes.

s: Cassander rules kingdom of Macedonia (owing to Antigonus)
q: And of the kings that put down the power of Antigonus I think the most unscrupulous was Cassander, who, having preserved his rule over the Macedonians only owing to Antigonus, went and fought against a man that had been his benefactor.

s: Cassander is beneficiary of Antigonus (his rule over the Macedonians depended on Antigonus)
q: Cassander, who, having preserved his rule over the Macedonians only owing to Antigonus, went and fought against a man that had been his benefactor.

s: Berenice is mother of Ptolemy
q: Now if this Ptolemy was really the son of Philip the son of Amyntas, it will be clear that he inherited this madness for women from his father, who, though married to Eurydice, the daughter of Antipater, and having children by her, yet fell in love with Berenice, (whom Antipater had sent into Egypt as a companion to Eurydice), and so enamoured was he of her that he had children by her, and when his end was near willed to reign over Egypt Ptolemy, (from whom the Athenians name one tribe), his son by Berenice and not by Eurydice.

s: Magas of Cyrene is son of Berenice
q: And when Cyrene revolted, Magas the son of Berenice, who was at this time the wife of Ptolemy, took it in the fifth year after the revolt.

s: Ptolemy is son of Lagus (putatively)
q: Ptolemy, the Macedonians think, was really the son of Philip the son of Amyntas, (but putatively the son of Lagus), for his mother, they say, was pregnant when she was given to Lagus to wife by Philip.

s: Philip is married to Eurydice (despite having children by her)
q: who, though married to Eurydice, the daughter of Antipater, and having children by her, yet fell in love with Berenice

s: Philip is father of Ptolemy (according to the account that Ptolemy was his son by Berenice)
q: when his end was near willed to reign over Egypt Ptolemy, (from whom the Athenians name one tribe), his son by Berenice and not by Eurydice.

s: Philip is father of children (by Eurydice)
q: who, though married to Eurydice, the daughter of Antipater, and having children by her

s: Philip is son of Amyntas
q: Ptolemy, the Macedonians think, was really the son of Philip the son of Amyntas, (but putatively the son of Lagus), for his mother, they say, was pregnant when she was given to Lagus to wife by Philip.

s: Alexander has satrap Cleomenes (in Egypt)
q: And he himself crossed into Egypt and slew Cleomenes, whom Alexander had made satrap of Egypt, thinking him friendly to Perdiccas and therefore not loyal to himself

s: Cleomenes is satrap of Egypt (appointed by Alexander)
q: And he himself crossed into Egypt and slew Cleomenes, whom Alexander had made satrap of Egypt, thinking him friendly to Perdiccas and therefore not loyal to himself

s: Alexander is son of Roxana (the lad Alexander, son of Alexander by Roxana)
q: Perdiccas, to give a specious colour to his expedition, led about with him Aridæus the son of Philip, and the lad Alexander, the son of Alexander by Roxana the daughter of Oxyartes

s: Perdiccas is opposed to Ptolemy (seeking the kingdom of Egypt)
q: Perdiccas, to give a specious colour to his expedition, led about with him Aridæus the son of Philip, and the lad Alexander, the son of Alexander by Roxana the daughter of Oxyartes, but really was plotting to take away the kingdom of Egypt from Ptolemy

s: Perdiccas is assassinated by Macedonians (his bodyguard)
q: But having been thrust out of Egypt, and consequently losing his former prestige as a general, and having incurred odium among the Macedonians on other grounds, he was assassinated by his bodyguard.

s: Zeus statue is a statue
q: The image of the god is in gold and ivory, seated on a throne.

s: throne of Zeus has contest between Hercules and the Amazons (represented in its remaining divisions; twenty-nine figures on each side)
q: And in the remaining divisions is the band of Hercules fighting against the Amazons. The number on each side is 29, and Theseus is on the side of Hercules.

s: throne of Zeus is supported by four pillars (between the four feet)
q: And the throne is supported not only by the four feet, but also by 4 pillars between the feet.

s: throne of Zeus is enclosed by panels like walls (at Olympia; preventing access beneath it)
q: But one cannot get under the throne, as one can at Amyclæ, and pass inside, for at Olympia there are panels like walls that keep one off.

s: Panænus is brother of Phidias
q: This Panænus was the brother of Phidias,

s: Hercules relieves Atlas (in the painting; willing to take over his load)
q: and Hercules standing by willing to relieve him of his load,

s: Hercules releases Prometheus (after slaying the eagle tormenting him)
q: For the tradition is that Hercules slew the eagle that was ever tormenting Prometheus on Mount Caucasus, and released Prometheus from his chains.

s: Zeus statue depicts Olympian Zeus
q: The image of the god is in gold and ivory, seated on a throne.

s: Phidias is brother of Panænus
q: This Panænus was the brother of Phidias,

s: Phidias is associated with the god (through the art of Phidias)
q: They make the god also to have testified to the art of Phidias.

s: Three Graces are daughters of Olympian Zeus (according to the poets)
q: For these too, as we learn from the poets, were daughters of Zeus.

s: Seasons are daughters of Olympian Zeus (according to the poets)
q: For these too, as we learn from the poets, were daughters of Zeus.

s: Homer wrote Iliad
q: Homer in the Iliad has represented the Seasons as having the care of Heaven, as a kind of guards of a royal palace.

s: Olympia contains Temple of Zeus at Olympia
q: At Olympia also in the temple of Zeus is a woollen veil, adorned with Assyrian tapestry and dyed with the Phœnician purple

s: black stone pavement is in front of Zeus statue (the entire pavement before the statue)
q: And all the pavement in front of the statue is not of white but of black stone.

s: Olympia uses oil (to protect the ivory of the Zeus statue from dampness)
q: For oil is good for the statue at Olympia, as it prevents the ivory being harmed by the dampness of the grove.

s: Zeus statue is made of gold and ivory
q: The image of the god is in gold and ivory, seated on a throne.

s: Antiochus dedicated woollen veil at Olympia (to Zeus at Olympia)
q: At Olympia also in the temple of Zeus is a woollen veil, adorned with Assyrian tapestry and dyed with the Phœnician purple, the votive offering of Antiochus,

s: Olympian Zeus holds Victory (in his right hand)
q: In his right hand he holds a Victory in ivory and gold, with a tiara and crown on his head: and in his left hand a sceptre adorned with all manner of precious stones, and the bird seated on the sceptre is an eagle.

s: Olympian games uses brazen shields (twenty-five, for competitors in the race in armour)
q: And there are 25 brazen shields to be worn by the competitors in the race in armour.

s: Pelops is honoured at Olympia (among the heroes; as highly as Zeus among the gods)
q: within Altis there is a separate grove to Pelops: who of the heroes at Olympia is as much held in the highest honour as Zeus is among the gods.

s: enclosure sacred to Pelops is dedicated by Hercules (according to tradition; Hercules son of Amphitryon)
q: And it is said to have been dedicated to Pelops by Hercules the son of Amphitryon, who was fourth in descent from Pelops.

s: enclosure sacred to Pelops is located near Temple of Zeus at Olympia (on its right toward the north)
q: This grove is on the right of the temple of Zeus towards the North, just at such a distance from the temple as to admit of statues and votive offerings between,

s: Pelops receives black ram (sacrificed annually by the magistrates)
q: And the magistrates for the year sacrifice to him even now a black ram.

s: Pelops is associated with Philoctetes (his shoulder-blade was brought to the Greek camp at Ilium)
q: So they sent it is said for Philoctetes to the camp, and the shoulder-blade of Pelops was brought from Pisa.

s: Olympian Zeus holds sceptre (in his left hand; adorned with precious stones and bearing an eagle)
q: In his right hand he holds a Victory in ivory and gold, with a tiara and crown on his head: and in his left hand a sceptre adorned with all manner of precious stones, and the bird seated on the sceptre is an eagle.

s: Pythian Priestess instructed Elis (to preserve the bones of Pelops)
q: And the Pythian Priestess told them to preserve the bones of Pelops, and told Damarmenus to give what he had found to the people of Elis.

s: altar of Olympian Zeus is 22 feet high
q: And the whole height of the altar is 22 feet.

s: Alpheus is considered friendly to Olympian Zeus (more than any other river)
q: No other water is ever used for this purpose, and that is why the Alpheus is considered more friendly to Olympian Zeus than any other river.

s: white poplar is used for Olympian altar ritual (as the only wood used by Elis in sacrifices to Zeus)
q: The wood of the white poplar tree is the only wood that the people of Elis employ in the sacrifices of Zeus,

s: Hercules introduced white poplar (from Thesprotia into Greece)
q: because Hercules introduced it from Thesprotia into Greece.

s: Zeus receives sacrifice (at Olympia to drive away flies)
q: when, either of his own idea or at another’s suggestion, he sacrificed to Zeus the Averter of flies, and so they were driven to the other side of the Alpheus

s: Olympian altar ritual begins with Vesta (in the order of Elis sacrifices)
q: They first sacrifice to Vesta, and next to Olympian Zeus in the altar inside the temple, thirdly to Hermes, fourthly to Artemis, fifthly to Athene the Goddess of Booty, sixthly to Athene Ergane.

s: Olympian Zeus is called altar of Olympian Zeus
q: With reference to the great altar, called the altar of Olympian Zeus, I have already spoken a little above.

s: Dionysus shares altar with Graces (in the grove of Pelops)
q: And in the grove of Pelops there is a joint altar to Dionysus and the Graces,

s: throne of Zeus is a throne
q: And the throne is richly adorned with gold and precious stones, and with ebony and ivory.

s: Muses has altar at enclosure sacred to Pelops
q: and next one to the Muses, and one to the Nymphs.

s: Nymphs has altar at enclosure sacred to Pelops
q: and next one to the Muses, and one to the Nymphs.

s: throne of Zeus is adorned with gold, precious stones, ebony, and ivory
q: And the throne is richly adorned with gold and precious stones, and with ebony and ivory.

s: throne of Zeus has Victory (four like dancers, one at each foot, and two at the instep of each foot)
q: There are four Victories like dancers one at each foot of the throne, and two also at the instep of each foot:

s: throne of Zeus has Theban boys (at each of the front feet, carried off by Sphinxes)
q: and at each of the front feet are Theban boys carried off by Sphinxes,

s: Mistresses has an altar at Altis
q: on the right of the Hall of Leonidas is an altar to the goddesses called Mistresses.

s: Arcadia contains information about Mistresses (in the narrator’s account)
q: Of the goddess whom they call Mistress the portion of my work about Arcadia will give complete information.

s: Poseidon has an altar at Olympia (in the open air at the middle of the starting-place)
q: And at the middle of the place where the horses start are altars in the open air to Poseidon the Patron of Horses, and Hera the Patroness of Horses

s: Hera the Patroness of Horses has an altar at Olympia (in the open air at the middle of the starting-place)
q: And at the middle of the place where the horses start are altars in the open air to Poseidon the Patron of Horses, and Hera the Patroness of Horses

s: Phidias worked at workshop of Phidias (at his statues)
q: Outside Altis there is a building called the workshop of Phidias, who used to work here at his statues, and there is an altar here to all the gods in common.

s: Town Hall of the people of Elis situated in Altis (near the outlet beyond the gymnasium)
q: And the Town Hall of the people of Elis is within Altis, near the outlet beyond the gymnasium, where the athletes have their races and wrestling-matches.

s: people of Elis sacrifice at sacrifices at the altars (once every month)
q: And once in every month the people of Elis sacrifice at the altars which I have mentioned.

s: sacrifices at the altars use frankincense (burned on the altars)
q: for they burn frankincense on the altars and cakes kneaded with honey.

s: sacrifices at the altars use cakes kneaded with honey (burned on the altars)
q: for they burn frankincense on the altars and cakes kneaded with honey.

s: people of Elis pour libations to god of Libya
q: And they pour libations not only to Greek gods, but to the god of Libya, and to Hera of Ammon, and to Parammon (a title of Hermes).

s: people of Elis consult oracle at Libya (from time immemorial)
q: It is manifest also that from time immemorial they have consulted the oracle at Libya

s: people of Elis honor heroes of Elis or Ætolia (and their wives)
q: The people of Elis also pour libations to heroes, and the wives of heroes, who are honoured in Elis or Ætolia.

s: temple of Hera is a Doric temple
q: Its architecture is Doric, there are pillars all round it, one pillar in a chamber at the back of the temple is of oak.

s: temple of Hera built by Scillus
q: The people of Elis have a tradition that the people of Scillus in Triphylia built it about 8 years after Oxylus became king at Elis.

s: Scillus located in Triphylia
q: the people of Scillus in Triphylia built it about 8 years after Oxylus became king at Elis.

s: temple of Hera dedicated to Hera
q: Next ought I to describe the temple of Hera, and all that is worth narrating in it.

s: Hera Festival presided over by sixteen matrons (every fifth year)
q: And every fifth year 16 matrons weave a shawl for Hera, and the same number preside over her games.

s: sixteen matrons weave shawl for Hera (every fifth year)
q: And every fifth year 16 matrons weave a shawl for Hera, and the same number preside over her games.

s: Hera’s maiden race is a race for maidens (at the Hera Festival)
q: And the contest is a race for maidens of various ages

s: Hera’s maiden race held at Olympia (on the regular race-course, shortened by a sixth of a stade)
q: They use in this contest the regular race-course at Olympia, but make it a sixth part of a stade shorter.

s: Hera’s maiden race awards olive crowns (to victors)
q: And the victors receive crowns of olive, and part of the heifer sacrificed to Hera

s: Hippodamia inaugurated Hera’s maiden race (in gratitude to Hera for her marriage with Pelops)
q: Hippodamia in gratitude to Hera for her marriage with Pelops selected 16 matrons, and in concert with them inaugurated these games to Hera.

s: Hippodamia married Pelops
q: Hippodamia in gratitude to Hera for her marriage with Pelops selected 16 matrons

s: Hall of Leonidas situated outside Altis (outside the temple precincts)
q: It is outside the temple precincts, and of the various approaches to Altis is the only one used for processions.

s: sixteen matrons selected from sixteen cities in Elis (one from each city)
q: so 16 of the principal cities in Elis at that day selected each one matron of age and merit and good name to arbitrate on any claims.

s: sixteen matrons chosen by people of Elis (two from each of eight tribes in the later arrangement)
q: For as they are divided into 8 tribes they select two matrons from each.

s: sixteen matrons holds two dances (the 16 matrons)
q: These 16 matrons also have two dances, one they call Physcoa’s dance, and the other’s Hippodamia’s.

s: Narcæus built Athene (a temple)
q: and built a temple of Athene Narcæa

s: Dionysus first worshipped by Narcæus
q: and Dionysus was they say first worshipped by Narcæus and Physcoa.

s: Dionysus first worshipped by Physcoa
q: and Dionysus was they say first worshipped by Narcæus and Physcoa.

s: Hall of Leonidas built by Leonidas
q: It was built by Leonidas, a native of Elis, and now the Roman governors of Elis make it their headquarters.

s: chest of Cypselus is a cedar chest (with figures in ivory, gold, and carved cedar)
q: The chest is of cedar and has figures on it, some in ivory, some in gold, some carved on the cedar.

s: Cypselus hid in chest of Cypselus (by his mother at birth)
q: In this chest Cypselus, the tyrant of Corinth, was hid by his mother at his birth

s: Cypselus is a tyrant (of Corinth)
q: In this chest Cypselus, the tyrant of Corinth, was hid by his mother at his birth

s: Cypselidæ descended from Cypselus (his descendants)
q: On account of his safety his descendants, called the Cypselidæ, made the chest a votive offering at Olympia

s: Cypselidæ dedicated chest of Cypselus (as a votive offering at Olympia)
q: his descendants, called the Cypselidæ, made the chest a votive offering at Olympia

s: chest of Cypselus has inscriptions in old Greek writing (including boustrophedon writing)
q: And on the chest there are inscriptions in large letters in an old handwriting: some of this writing is straight, other parts are written in what the Greeks call ox-fashion.

s: Hercules is depicted in chest of Cypselus (shooting the hydra)
q: And there is Athene standing by Hercules who is shooting the hydra, the monster that infested the river Amymone.

s: Leonidas native of Elis
q: It was built by Leonidas, a native of Elis, and now the Roman governors of Elis make it their headquarters.

s: hydra infested river Amymone (as a monster)
q: the hydra, the monster that infested the river Amymone.

s: Olympian games have victors entertained at banquet for Olympic victors (in the Town Hall)
q: The people of Elis also have a banqueting-hall, (inside the Town-Hall, opposite the room where the hearth is,) where they entertain the victors at Olympia.

s: Olympia awards crowns from olive beautiful for its crowns (to victors)
q: it is called the olive beautiful for its crowns, and the victors at Olympia receive crowns of it.

s: Menelaus pursues Helen (to kill her during the sack of Ilium)
q: And there is Menelaus with a breastplate and sword pursuing Helen to kill her, plainly during the sack of Ilium.

s: Jason woos Medea
q: “Jason is wooing Medea, Aphrodite is encouraging them.”

s: Aphrodite encourages Jason (in wooing Medea)
q: “Jason is wooing Medea, Aphrodite is encouraging them.”

s: Muses sing Apollo (Apollo leads them in the songs)
q: The Muses are also represented singing and Apollo leading off, and the inscription is as follows,

s: Apollo leads Muses (in songs)
q: And round him the Muses, a graceful band, whom he leads in the songs.”

s: Leto is parent of Apollo
q: “Here is the king, the son of Leto, far-darting Apollo,

s: Hercules approaches Atlas (with a sword; inferred from the representation)
q: And who the man is with a sword advancing to Atlas is nowhere written, but it is evident to all that it is Hercules.

s: Ares leads away Aphrodite (in full armour)
q: There is also Ares in full armour leading off Aphrodite. The inscription under him is Enyalius.

s: Perseus is pursued by Medusa (by her winged sisters)
q: And there are the sisters of Medusa with wings pursuing the fleeing Perseus.

s: Elis is related to Ætolians (according to one antiquarian explanation, through ancient consanguinity)
q: the one party say that it is the Ætolians with Oxylus and the ancient people of Elis, and that they are fraternizing and exhibiting friendliness to one another in remembrance of their ancient consanguinity

s: Pylos fights Arcadians (near Pheia and the river Iardanus, according to one explanation)
q: the other party say that it is the people of Pylos and the Arcadians fighting near the town of Pheia and the river Iardanus.

s: Cypselus is a descendant of Melas (through his ancestors)
q: Cypselus and his ancestors came originally from Gonussa beyond Sicyon, and were descended from Melas the son of Antasus.

s: Achilles fights Memnon (their mothers stand by)
q: And Achilles and Memnon are fighting and their mothers are standing by.

s: Strife stands by Ajax (at his duel with Hector after challenge; depicted as hateful)
q: And Strife, looking most hateful, stands by the duel (after challenge) between Ajax and Hector.

s: Æthra is a daughter of Pittheus (wearing a dark dress)
q: And Æthra, the daughter of Pittheus, in a dark dress is prostrate on the ground at the feet of Helen.

s: Hermes brings Hera (to Paris for the choice of beauty)
q: And Hermes is bringing to Paris, the son of Priam, the goddesses to the choice of beauty

s: Artemis has wings (on her shoulders)
q: And Artemis--I know not why--has wings on her shoulders, and in her right hand she has a leopard, in her left a lion.

s: Artemis possesses leopard (in her right hand)
q: And Artemis--I know not why--has wings on her shoulders, and in her right hand she has a leopard, in her left a lion.

s: Artemis possesses lion (in her left hand)
q: And Artemis--I know not why--has wings on her shoulders, and in her right hand she has a leopard, in her left a lion.

s: Dionysus possesses golden bowl (while lying in a cave)
q: And there too is bearded Dionysus lying down in a cave, clad in a long garment, with a golden bowl in his hand: and there are clusters of vine round him, and apples, and pomegranates.

s: Odysseus is with Circe (sleeping with her on a bed in a cave)
q: In a cave there is a woman sleeping with a man upon a bed, and we infer that they are Odysseus and Circe from the number of handmaids in front of the cave, and from their tasks.

s: Eumelus is suspected of constructing chest of Cypselus
q: Who it was that constructed this chest it is quite impossible to conjecture: the inscriptions on it might have been composed by anybody, but suspicion points to Eumelus the Corinthian

s: Iphitus possesses quoit (the quoit bears the armistice inscription around it)
q: There are also here besides the chest several votive offerings, as a bed of no great size adorned with much ivory, and the quoit of Iphitus

s: Olympians has armistice with Elis (written around Iphitus’ quoit)
q: the quoit of Iphitus has written on it the armistice between the people of Elis and the Olympians not straight down it, but all round the quoit

s: temple of Hera is a Doric temple (large in size)
q: The temple, which is large in size and of Doric architecture, they call to this day the Temple of the Mother

s: Altis contains Temple of the Mother (the temple is inside Altis)
q: It is inside Altis, and there is a round building called Philip’s House

s: Philip has Philip’s House (built for him after the defeat at Chæronea)
q: It was built for Philip after the fatal defeat of the Greeks at Chæronea.

s: Alexander is depicted at Philip’s House (in ivory and gold by Leochares)
q: And there are statues there of Philip, and Alexander, and Amyntas the father of Philip. They are by Leochares in ivory and gold

s: Eupolus bribes Agenor of Arcadia (to let him win boxing at Olympia)
q: For Eupolus the Thessalian bribed his rivals in boxing to let him win the prize, Agenor from Arcadia, and Prytanis from Cyzicus, and Phormio from Halicarnassus

s: Eupolus is fined for bribery at Olympia (by the people of Elis)
q: This was the first foul play they say at the boxing matches, and Eupolus and those who had been bribed by him were fined by the people of Elis.

s: Olympian games require merit (not money, according to the inscription on the Zanes)
q: And the fourth desires to point out that the contest at Olympia is one of merit and not of money.

s: Delphi orders Athenians (to pay Callippus’ fine to Elis)
q: till the god at Delphi told them he would no longer give them any oracular responses, till they paid the fine to the people of Elis.

s: Straton of Alexandria wins pancratium (in the 178th Olympiad, according to Elis’ public records)
q: For in these records they say that Straton of Alexandria in the 178th Olympiad won on the same day the prize both in the pancratium and in the wrestling.

s: Apollo snatches away Marpessa (for himself)
q: “Idas is leading away from the temple by no means against her will Marpessa of the beautiful ancles, whom Apollo snatched away for himself.”

s: Zeus assumes appearance of Amphitryon (in the Greek tradition)
q: According to the Greek tradition, Zeus assumed the appearance of Amphitryon, and so made Alcmena welcome him as her husband.

s: Alcmena welcomes Zeus (as her husband while he appears as Amphitryon)
q: According to the Greek tradition, Zeus assumed the appearance of Amphitryon, and so made Alcmena welcome him as her husband.

s: statues of Zeus are located in Altis
q: Such are the statues of Zeus inside Altis, all of which I have enumerated.

s: statues of Zeus are erected some erected publicly, some privately
q: Such are the statues made out of fines as far as I could ascertain. There are also other statues of Zeus, some erected publicly, some privately.

s: Greeks who fought at Platæa erected Zeus (a statue at Olympia)
q: This is towards the East, and was erected by the Greeks who fought at Platæa against Mardonius and the Medes.

s: Battle of Platæa was fought against Mardonius (by the Greeks who fought at Platæa)
q: This is towards the East, and was erected by the Greeks who fought at Platæa against Mardonius and the Medes.

s: inscribed list of the Greek allies lists Lacedæmonians (first among the participating states)
q: On the right of the basement are inscribed the states that took part in the action, the Lacedæmonians first, and next the Athenians

s: inscribed list of the Greek allies lists Athenians (second among the participating states)
q: On the right of the basement are inscribed the states that took part in the action, the Lacedæmonians first, and next the Athenians

s: Mycenæ was destroyed by Argives (after the Persian war)
q: Mycenæ and Tiryns were razed to the ground by the Argives after the Persian war.

s: Tiryns was destroyed by Argives (after the Persian war)
q: Mycenæ and Tiryns were razed to the ground by the Argives after the Persian war.

s: 30-year peace between Sparta and Athens was between Lacedæmonians (and Athenians)
q: There is also in front of this statue of Zeus a brazen pillar, on which are inscribed the conditions of peace for 30 years between the Lacedæmonians and the Athenians

s: 30-year peace between Sparta and Athens excluded Argives (from participation in the peace)
q: that the city of the Argives should have no share in this peace between the Athenians and Lacedæmonians

s: Council Chamber statue of Zeus is called Zeus the God of Oaths (the most terrifying statue of Zeus)
q: But the statue of Zeus in the Council Chamber is of all the statues of Zeus most calculated to frighten wicked men, his Title is Zeus the God of Oaths

s: Council Chamber statue of Zeus holds two thunderbolts (one in each hand)
q: and he has a thunderbolt in each hand.

s: Olympic athletes swear over oath over the entrails of a boar (not to cheat at the Olympian games)
q: At this statue it is customary for the athletes, their fathers and brothers, and also their trainers, to swear over the entrails of a boar that they will not cheat at the Olympian games.

s: Umpires of Elis swears to give their decisions honestly and without bribes
q: And the umpires also, either of boys or the colts that compete in the races, swear to give their decisions honestly and without bribes, and not to reveal the reasons for their selection of the winners.

s: brazen tablet of Zeus the God of Oaths is located before Council Chamber statue of Zeus (at the feet of the statue)
q: And before the feet of Zeus the God of Oaths there is a brazen tablet, on which some elegiac lines are inscribed, that are meant to inspire fear in perjurers.

s: Messenians at the Sicilian Strait sent chorus of thirty-five boys (to Rhegium for the national feast)
q: The Messenians at the Sicilian Strait, who used to send to Rhegium, according to old custom, a chorus of 35 boys and a choir-master and a piper to the national feast

s: chorus of thirty-five boys was destroyed in shipwreck in the Sicilian Strait (with none surviving)
q: had on one occasion a terrible disaster, none of those that were sent were saved, but the vessel that had the boys on board perished boys and all in the depths of the sea.

s: brazen effigies of the drowned chorus were made by Callon of Elis
q: The effigies were by Callon of Elis.

s: Sicilian Strait is formed by Sicilian Sea (together with the Tyrrhenian Sea)
q: winds lash it to fury, and two seas meet, the Sicilian and the Tyrrhenian

s: Hercules is depicted in a votive offering of Hercules
q: The Thasians also (who were Phœnicians originally, and sailed from Tyre and other parts of Phœnice to Europe with Thasus the son of Agenor), made a votive offering of Hercules at Olympia

s: Hercules is depicted holding club (in the right hand of the Thasian statue)
q: The height of the statue is 10 cubits, in the right hand he holds his club, and in the left his bow.

s: Hercules is depicted holding bow (in the left hand of the Thasian statue)
q: The height of the statue is 10 cubits, in the right hand he holds his club, and in the left his bow.

s: Achæans has statues of those who, when Hector challenged a single Greek to single combat, drew lots (from the Achæan race in common)
q: There are also statues, from the Achæan race in common, of those who, when Hector challenged a single Greek to single combat, drew lots who it should be.

s: Onatas the Æginetan made Hercules (the Thasian votive offering at Olympia)
q: Onatas the son of Micon made me, a dweller at Ægina.

s: Onatas the Æginetan is regarded as great sculptor (second to none since Dædalus and the Attic school)
q: This Æginetan Onatas we should regard in the statuary art as second to none since Dædalus and the Attic school.

s: semicircular basement near the Hippodamium is located near Hippodamium
q: And near what is called the Hippodamium there is a semicircular basement of stone, and statues on it of Zeus and Thetis and Aurora supplicating Zeus for their children.

s: semicircular basement near the Hippodamium contains Achilles (at one extremity, facing Memnon)
q: And at each extremity of the basement stand Achilles and Memnon in the attitude of antagonists.

s: Messenians received Naupactus (from the Athenians)
q: The Dorian Messenians also, who received Naupactus from the Athenians, erected at Olympia a Victory on a pillar

s: Micythus lived at Tegea (after Anaxilas’s death)
q: and after his death went to Tegea

s: Micythus is son of Chœrus (according to the inscriptions)
q: And the inscriptions on these votive offerings make Micythus the son of Chœrus

s: Micythus is native of Rhegium (the inscriptions call it the Greek colony of Rhegium)
q: and the Greek colony of Rhegium, or Messene near the Strait, his native place

s: Micythus is native of Messene near the Strait (alternative designation in the inscriptions)
q: and the Greek colony of Rhegium, or Messene near the Strait, his native place

s: Micythus dedicated votive offerings (at Olympia for the recovery of his son)
q: these votive offerings at Olympia were the fulfilment of a vow for the recovery of his son, who was wasting away in a consumption

s: Micythus places Proserpine the daughter of Demeter (near the left side of the great temple)
q: And near the left side of the great temple he placed Proserpine the daughter of Demeter

s: Micythus dedicated Aphrodite (among his votive offerings)
q: And near the left side of the great temple he placed Proserpine the daughter of Demeter, and Aphrodite, and Ganymede, and Artemis

s: Micythus dedicated Ganymede (among his votive offerings)
q: And near the left side of the great temple he placed Proserpine the daughter of Demeter, and Aphrodite, and Ganymede, and Artemis

s: Micythus dedicated Artemis (among his votive offerings)
q: And near the left side of the great temple he placed Proserpine the daughter of Demeter, and Aphrodite, and Ganymede, and Artemis

s: Messenians erected Victory (at Olympia)
q: The Dorian Messenians also, who received Naupactus from the Athenians, erected at Olympia a Victory on a pillar

s: Micythus dedicated Homer (among his votive offerings)
q: and of the poets Homer and Hesiod

s: Micythus dedicated Hesiod (among his votive offerings)
q: and of the poets Homer and Hesiod

s: Micythus dedicated Æsculapius (among his votive offerings)
q: and of the gods again Æsculapius and Hygiea

s: Micythus dedicated Hygiea (among his votive offerings)
q: and of the gods again Æsculapius and Hygiea

s: Micythus dedicated Agon (with dumb bells)
q: And among the votive offerings of Micythus is Agon with the dumb bells.

s: Phormis is a Mænalian (from Mænalus)
q: Mænalian Phormis, who crossed over from Mænalus to Sicily to Gelon the son of Dinomenes

s: Phormis served under Gelon (in Gelon’s army)
q: and in the army of Gelon, and afterwards in the army of Gelon’s brother Hiero, displayed great valour

s: Victory is a Victory (on a pillar)
q: erected at Olympia a Victory on a pillar

s: Phormis served under Hiero (in Hiero’s army)
q: and afterwards in the army of Gelon’s brother Hiero, displayed great valour
